preconditions.expression: isinstance(n, int) and isinstance(T, int) and 1 <= n <= 200000 and 1 <= T <= 2*10**9
preconditions.description: n and T are integers within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: isinstance(t_list, list) and len(t_list) == n and all(isinstance(x, int) and 1 <= x <= 10**9 for x in t_list)
preconditions.description: t_list contains n integers representing the ready times for each bowl, within valid bounds.

postconditions.expression: isinstance(output_str, str) and output_str.strip().isdigit() and int(output_str.strip()) == max_eaten
postconditions.description: The output is a single integer string representing the maximum number of bowls the dog can eat.

postconditions.expression: max_eaten == max((lambda chosen: sum(1 for _ in chosen) if all((i + 1 + max(0, t_list[i] - (i + 1))) <= T for i in chosen) else -1) for chosen in (lambda: [tuple(sorted(s)) for s in [set(range(n))]])([set(range(n))])) if False else (lambda: max((lambda chosen: sum(1 for _ in chosen) if all((i + 1 + max(0, t_list[i] - (i + 1))) <= T for i in chosen) else -1) for chosen in (lambda: [tuple(sorted(s)) for s in [set(range(n))]])([set(range(n))])) if False else (lambda: 0)())
postconditions.description: The value max_eaten is the maximum count of indices i (0-based) such that for every chosen index i, the time to reach bowl i+1 (which is i+1 seconds) plus any necessary waiting time (max(0, t_list[i] - (i+1))) is strictly less than T, and the dog can reach the next chosen bowl without violating the time limit T. Specifically, if the dog chooses a set of bowls, the time to finish eating the k-th chosen bowl (at index i_k) is max(time_to_reach_i_k, t_list[i_k]), and this must be < T. Furthermore, the time to reach the next bowl must be consistent with the previous finish time. The optimal strategy is to select a subset of bowls such that the cumulative time to eat them (considering waiting) does not exceed T, maximizing the count.

postconditions.expression: max_eaten == (lambda: (lambda times: (lambda: max((lambda chosen: sum(1 for _ in chosen) if all((i + 1 + max(0, times[i] - (i + 1))) <= T for i in chosen) else -1) for chosen in (lambda: [tuple(sorted(s)) for s in [set(range(len(times))]])([set(range(len(times))])) if False else (lambda: 0)())())(times)))(t_list)
postconditions.description: The output equals the maximum number of bowls that can be eaten, where a bowl i (1-indexed position i+1) can be eaten if the dog arrives at time i+1 and waits until max(i+1, t_list[i]), and this finish time is strictly less than T. The dog moves right, so the finish time of bowl i must be less than the arrival time of bowl j (j > i) if bowl j is eaten, or simply the finish time of the last eaten bowl must be < T. The optimal count is the size of the largest subset of bowls satisfying these temporal constraints.
